extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX/TikZ/PGF users creating diagrams, Petri nets, plots, and shapes
extracted.subtask_description: Reference guidance for using TikZ/PGF: node styles for Petri nets (places, transitions, tokens), plot handlers and marks, predefined shapes, and the snake/to-path libraries. Covers options, defaults, and recommended parameters for drawing and layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: label option for node exterior text
rubrics_metrics.description: You should use the label option to add text outside the node like its name or its capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For node names or capacity annotations place text with label=... (e.g. label=above:$p_1$). Do not place such exterior text as the node's core content if you want it outside the border.

rubrics_metrics.name: tokens option for tokens inside a place
rubrics_metrics.description: You should use the tokens options, explained in Section 27.3, to add tokens inside the place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a place node tokens=<number> or use children are tokens to have tokens appear inside the place rather than adding separate token nodes manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every place to change place appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: style=every place This style is envoked by the style place. To change the appearance of places, you can change this style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redefine \tikzstyle{every place} (or every place option) to change fill, draw, minimum size, thickness etc. Example: \tikzstyle{every place}=[draw=blue,fill=blue!20,thick,minimum size=9mm].

rubrics_metrics.name: places should use label for external text and tokens for internals
rubrics_metrics.description: As for places, the text of a transition should be empty and the label option should be used for adding labels. (Applies similarly to places: put external text in label and internal tokens via tokens option.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the node body empty for places/transitions and use label=... for captions; use tokens/children are tokens for depiction of tokens inside places.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=transition indicates transition nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: style=transition This style indicates that a node is a transition. As for places, the text of a transition should be empty and the label option should be used for adding labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \node[transition,label=below:$t_1$] {}; to create transitions. Treat transitions as nodes with empty content and labels outside.

rubrics_metrics.name: use edge (to) with pre/post styles to connect transitions and places
rubrics_metrics.description: To connect a transition to places, you can use the edge command as in the example; use styles pre/post to indicate pre-set/post-set membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: edge[pre] (p1) or edge[post] node[auto]{2} (p2). Use edge or to with styles pre/post to make arcs semantically clear and style-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every transition to change transition appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: style=every transition This style is envoked by the style transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redefine every transition to change how all transitions look (stroke, fill, shape, minimum size).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=pre default arrow and redefinability
rubrics_metrics.description: style=pre This style can be used with paths leading from a transition to a place to indicate that the place is in the pre-set of the transition. By default, this style is <-,shorten <=1pt, but feel free to redefine it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may change the arrow direction, arrow head, shortening, and other path properties by redefining style=pre.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=post for post-set arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: style=post This style is also used with paths leading from a transition to a place, but this time the place is in the post-set of the transition. Again, feel free to redefine it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use or redefine style=post analogously to pre to control visual appearance of output arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=pre and post for places in both pre- and post-set
rubrics_metrics.description: style=pre and post This style is to be used to indicate that a place is both in the pre- and post-set of a transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine or provide a distinct style to show self-loops or places that are both consumed and produced by a transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=token indicates a token node
rubrics_metrics.description: style=token This style indicates that a node is a token. By default, this causes the node to be a small black circle. Unlike places and transitions, it does make sense to provide text for the token node. Such text will be typeset in a tiny font and in white on black (naturally, you can easily change this by setting the style every token).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use token nodes for custom token appearances; change every token to alter default token size, color, font, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: children are tokens style for placing multiple tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: style=children are tokens The idea behind this style is to use trees mechanism for placing tokens. Every token lying on a place is treated as a child of the node. The children are tokens style redefines the growth function of trees such that it places the children next to each other inside (on top of) the place node and hides the edge from the parent node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use [children are tokens] and child {node[token] {...}} constructs to place multiple tokens inside a place without manual positioning. Avoid default tree behavior (below the node) because this style repositions tokens inside the place.

rubrics_metrics.name: children are tokens maps placements for up to nine tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: The special tree growth function for tokens has a special mapping for each possible number of children up to nine children. This mapping decides for each child where it should be placed on top of the place. ... If you wish to place more than nine tokens on a place, you will have to write your own placement code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Built-in placement covers 1..9 tokens (single center, 2 side-by-side, 3 triangle, etc.). For 10+ tokens, implement custom placement logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: token distance option
rubrics_metrics.description: token distance=... This specifies the distance between the centers of the tokens in the arrangements of the option children are tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune token_distance (e.g. token distance=1.1ex) to increase/decrease spacing between tokens in multi-token arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: tokens=number place option
rubrics_metrics.description: tokens=number This option is given to a place node, not to a token node. The effect of this option is to add number many child nodes to the place, each having the style token.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tokens=3 is shorthand for adding three child token nodes under children are tokens. tokens=0 is legal and draws no tokens. Note: this option does not handle 10 or more tokens correctly (see children are tokens remark).

rubrics_metrics.name: colored tokens place option
rubrics_metrics.description: colored tokens=color list This option, which must also be given when a place node is being created, gets a list of colors as parameter. It will then add as many tokens to the place are in this list, each colored with the corresponding color in the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use e.g. colored tokens={black,black,red,blue} to create multicolored tokens. This uses children are tokens internally, so every token style changes apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: structured tokens place option
rubrics_metrics.description: structured tokens=token texts This option, which must again be passed to a place, gets a list texts for tokens. For each text, another token will be added to the place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured tokens={$x$,$y$,$z$} to label individual tokens. If you use lots of structured tokens, consider redefining every token style so tokens are larger.

rubrics_metrics.name: tokens=0 legal; tokens option limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is legal to say tokens=0, no tokens are drawn in this case. This option does not handle ten or more tokens correctly. If you need this many tokens, you will have to program your own code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tokens=0 to explicitly show an empty place. For 10+ tokens implement custom placement or code.

rubrics_metrics.name: use children are tokens internally by convenience options
rubrics_metrics.description: The children are tokens options gives you a lot of flexibility, but it is a bit cumbersome to use. For this reason there are some options that help in standard situations. They all use children are tokens internally, so any change to, say, the every tokens style will affect how these options depict tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience options (tokens=, colored tokens=, structured tokens=) wrap children are tokens; modifying every token affects their display.

rubrics_metrics.name: curve plot handler uses tension scaled control vectors
rubrics_metrics.description:
The curve plot handler (
pgfplothandlercurveto) generates control points automatically: to determine the control points at point y (with neighbors x and z), the handler computes the vector z − x and scales it by the tension factor. Let s be that vector; then y+s and y−s are control points around y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control curve shape by changing plot tension via \pgfsetplottension{value}. Higher tension increases curvature; default 0.5; value 1 connects quarter-circle points.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsetplottension to control curve curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsetplottension{value} Sets the factor used by the curve plot handlers to determine the distance of the control points from the points they control. The higher the curvature of the curve points, the higher this value should be. A value of 1 will cause four points at quarter positions of a circle to be connected using a circle. The default is 0.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune tension depending on desired curvature: default 0.5, increase toward 1 for stronger curvature. Examples show 0.75, 1.0 behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: closed curve plot handler
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfplothandlerclosedcurve This handler works like the curve-to plot handler, only it will add a new part to the current path that is a closed curve through the plot points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use closedcurve when you want smooth closed shapes passing through points rather than open Bézier curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: comb plot handlers (xcomb, ycomb, polarcomb)
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfplothandlerxcomb/\pgfplothandlerycomb/\pgfplothandlerpolarcomb convert each point into a line from a reference axis/origin to the point's coordinate, producing comb-like plots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: xcomb creates horizontal combs (lines from y-axis), ycomb creates vertical combs (lines from x-axis) useful for bar diagrams; polarcomb draws lines from origin to points for radial combs.

rubrics_metrics.name: mark plot handler executes mark code at point origin
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfplothandlermark{mark code} This command will execute the mark code for some points of the plot, but each time the coordinate transformation matrix will be setup such that the origin is at the position of the point to be plotted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly used mark code is \pgfuseplotmark{mark name}. By default marks are drawn at all points but can be controlled by repeat/phase/index list.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsetplotmarkrepeat and \pgfsetplotmarkphase control mark frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsetplotmarkrepeat{repeat} Sets the r parameter to repeat, that is, only every rth mark will be drawn. \pgfsetplotmarkphase{phase} Sets the p parameter to phase, that is, the first mark to be drawn is the pth, followed by (p+r)th, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeat and phase to decimate marks (e.g., only every 5th mark) and to offset where marking starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: marklisted to place marks at explicit indices
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfplothandlermarklisted{mark code}{index list} Works similar to mark but places marks only at indices in index list (syntax same as \foreach), e.g. 1,3,...,25 or 1,2,4,8,16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use marklisted to plot marks at a custom sequence of indices or powers-of-two etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfuseplotmark to draw declared plot marks
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfuseplotmark{plot mark name} Draws the given plot mark name at the origin. The plot mark name must previously have been declared using \pgfdeclareplotmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare marks with \pgfdeclareplotmark and then draw them with \pgfuseplotmark inside a mark handler.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfdeclareplotmark to define custom marks
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfdeclareplotmark{plot mark name}{code} Declares a plot mark for later use with the \pgfuseplotmark command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide code where origin corresponds to point; mark code may draw using \pgfpath... and \pgfusepath{stroke}/fill. Example shows a custom 'my plot mark' drawing a circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsetplotmarksize recommendation dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsetplotmarksize{dimension} This command sets the TeX dimension \pgfplotmarksize to dimension. This dimension is a 'recommendation' for plot mark code at which size the plot mark should be drawn; plot mark code may choose to ignore this dimension altogether. For circles, dimension should be the radius, for other shapes it should be about half the width/height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set \pgfsetplotmarksize{1ex} to influence predefined and custom marks; remember it's only a recommendation and custom mark code may ignore it.

rubrics_metrics.name: predefined plot marks list
rubrics_metrics.description: The following plot marks are predefined (the filling color has been set to yellow): *, x, + and additional marks -, |, o, asterisk, star, oplus, oplus*, otimes, otimes*, square, square*, triangle, triangle*, diamond, diamond*, pentagon, pentagon*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these predefined names with \pgfuseplotmark{...} inside mark handlers for standard mark shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: diamond shape aspect ratio and anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape diamond: This shape is a diamond tightly fitting the text box. The ratio between width and height is 1 by default, but can be changed by setting the shape aspect ratio (using the aspect option of TikZ). Anchors (including border anchors) are defined for precise placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set aspect option to change width:height; use anchors like (s.north), (s.10), (s.130) to attach things to precise border points.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellipse shape fits text box and anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape ellipse: This shape is an ellipse tightly fitting the text box if no inner separation is given. The shape defines many anchors including base, mid, text, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ellipse for rounded nodes that conform to content. Use anchors (s.base west, s.mid west, etc.) for positioning and annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: regular polygon border based on incircle; size semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular polygon: The border is constructed using the incircle (circle that touches every side). The radius of the incircle is calculated to tightly fit the node contents. If the node is enlarged to minimum size/width/height, this is interpreted as the diameter of the circumcircle (circle through all corners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that minimum size interprets diameter of circumcircle; to control number of sides use \pgfsetpolygonsides or regular polygon sides option; rotation via \pgfsetpolygonrotate or regular polygon rotate option.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsetpolygonsides and rotate for polygons
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsetpolygonsides{integer} Set the number of sides for the polygon. \pgfsetpolygonrotate{angle} Rotate the border of the polygon independently of the node contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative TikZ options: regular polygon sides=<n> and regular polygon rotate=<angle> to control polygon appearance declaratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: star shape inner/outer point semantics and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape star: A star has inner points and outer points. The inner points of the border are based on the radius of the circle which tightly fits the node contents. Any specified minimum size, width or height is interpreted as the diameter of the circle that passes through every outer point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control star geometry using star points, star point height, star point ratio, and star rotate to adjust number of points, point height, radii ratio, and rotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: star parameter commands and options
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsetstarpoints{integer}, \pgfsetstarpointheight{distance}, \pgfsetstarpointratio{number}, \pgfsetstarrotate{angle} and TikZ options star points=, star point height=, star point ratio=, star rotate= set respective star parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune star point height (distance between inner and outer radii) and star point ratio (outer/inner radius factor). When scaling via minimum size, inner radius adjusts to maintain point height/ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: forbidden sign symbol shape layering and anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape forbidden sign: This shape places the node inside a circle with a diagonal from the lower left to the upper right added. The circle is part of the background, the diagonal line part of the foreground path; thus, the diagonal line is on top of the text. The shape inherits all anchors from the circle shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forbidden sign for pictograms like 'No Smoking'. Control line width and colors (e.g., line width=1ex, draw=red).

rubrics_metrics.name: multipart shapes (circle split) with nodepart
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape circle split: This shape is a multi-part shape consisting of a circle with a line in the middle. The upper part is the main part (text part), the lower part is the lower part. It defines \nodepart{lower} and a lower anchor in addition to circle anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \node[shape=circle split]{upper \nodepart{lower} lower}; to separate text into upper/lower parts and address anchors like (s.lower) for positioning elements relative to the lower part.

rubrics_metrics.name: cross out/strike out shapes for inline text
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape cross out draws two diagonal lines between corners of the node’s bounding box; shape strike out draws a single diagonal line from lower left to upper right. Useful inline with text via \tikz[baseline] \node[cross out,draw,anchor=text]{me};
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These shapes inherit rectangle anchors. Use them inline to cross/strike words while maintaining baseline alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake library parameter convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The snakes are influenced by the current values of parameters like \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude. Only this parameter and \pgfsnakesegmentlength are proper TeX dimensions, all other parameters are TeX macros. In TikZ, each parameter can be set using an option having the parameter's name minus the \pgfsnake part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set snake parameters in TikZ via options such as segment amplitude=..., segment length=..., segment aspect=.... Remember which are dimensions vs macros when manipulating at TeX level.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=bent parameters: segment amplitude and aspect
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake bent: This snake adds a slightly bent line from the start to the target. The amplitude of the bent is given by the segment amplitude (and amplitude of zero gives a straight line). • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines the amplitude of the bent. • \pgfsnakesegmentaspect determines how tight the bent is. A good value is around 0.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use segment amplitude to control bend size and segment aspect~0.3 for typical bent shapes. Example: \draw[->,snake=bent,raise snake=2pt] (A) -- (B);

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=border parameters: length, amplitude, angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake border: adds straight ticks to the path at a specific angle to the line toward the target. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines distance between consecutive ticks. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines length of ticks. • \pgfsnakesegmentangle determines the angle between ticks and line toward the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use segment length/amplitude/angle to shape border ticks. Example: [snake=border,segment angle=-45].

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=brace parameters: amplitude and aspect
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake brace: adds a long brace to the path; left and right end are exactly start and end. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines how much the brace rises above the path. • \pgfsnakesegmentaspect determines fraction of total length where the 'middle part' of the brace will be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune amplitude and aspect to control brace height and midpoint location (e.g., segment aspect=0.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=bumps parameters: amplitude and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake bumps: consists of little half ellipses. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines the height of the half ellipse. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the width of the half ellipse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust segment amplitude and length to get desired bump size and spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=coil parameters: amplitude, length, aspect (viewing direction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake coil: adds a coil to the path. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude is the coil radius. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength is distance between consecutive 'curls' (wavelength when seen from side). • \pgfsnakesegmentaspect determines 'viewing direction' (0: side view -> sine; 0.5 default: more front view).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune amplitude/length/aspect to produce coils of desired radius, curl spacing, and apparent perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=expanding waves parameters: length and angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake expanding waves: adds arcs to the path that get bigger along the line; • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the distance between consecutive arcs. • \pgfsnakesegmentangle determines the opening angle below and above the path (total opening is twice this angle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use segment length and segment angle to control spacing and arc aperture in expanding wave snakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=saw parameters: amplitude and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake saw: looks like the blade of a saw. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines how much each spike raises above the straight line. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the length each spike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set amplitude and length to control spike height and width for sawtooth decorations.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=snake (sine-like) parameters: amplitude and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake snake: the 'archetypical' snake: a sine wave with a 'softened' start and ending. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines the sine wave's amplitude. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the sine wave's wave length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune amplitude and length to control the sine wave's amplitude and wavelength; use for decorative wavy lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=ticks parameters: length and amplitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake ticks: adds straight lines orthogonal to the line toward the target. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines distance between consecutive ticks. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines half the length of the ticks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust segment length & amplitude to control tick spacing and size; useful for markings along paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=triangles parameters: length, amplitude, objectlength
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake triangles: adds triangles to the path that point toward the target. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines distance between consecutive triangles. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines half the length of the triangle side orthogonal to path. • \pgfsnakesegmentobjectlength determines the height of the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these three parameters to control spacing, base half-width, and triangle height for arrow-like decorations.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=crosses parameters: length, amplitude, objectlength
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake crosses: adds diagonal crosses to the path. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines spacing between crosses. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines half the height of each cross. • \pgfsnakesegmentobjectlength determines width of each cross.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune parameters to control cross spacing and size; useful for patterned path decorations.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=waves parameters: length, angle, amplitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake waves: adds arcs to the path with constant size. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines distance between consecutive arcs. • \pgfsnakesegmentangle determines opening angle below and above the path (total opening twice this). • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines the radius of each arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control arc spacing, aperture and radius to produce periodic arc decorations.

rubrics_metrics.name: snake=zigzag parameters: amplitude and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Snake zigzag: looks like a zig-zag line. • \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude determines how much the zig-zag raises above and falls below a straight line to the target point. • \pgfsnakesegmentlength determines the length of a complete 'up-down' cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust amplitude and length to set zigzag amplitude and period; useful for stylized jagged connectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: to-path library 'line to' and 'curve to' styles
rubrics_metrics.description: style=line to causes a straight line to be added to the path upon a to or an edge operation. style=curve to specifies that the to path should be a curve leaving the start at angle out=... and reaching target at angle in=.... Control points depend on options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to[line to] for straight connections, to[curve to] with out= and in= angles to create curved edges; control curve shape via additional options (out=, in=, tension, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: out= and in= angles for curve endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: out=angle The angle at which the curve leaves the start coordinate. If the start coordinate is a node, the start coordinate is the point on the border of the node at the given angle. in=angle The angle at which the curve reaches the target coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify out=45,in=135 to control tangent directions of the curve at start and end; when nodes are involved the point is on node border at that angle.
